messages:
Olivia: FYI — last night at ~09:12 UTC we hit a sharp sustained queue spike in us-west-2 after a partner batch burst. queue_len peaked ~420, admission_rejects spiked. seeing a lot of 429 + downstream tail latency.
Marc: Confirmed in metrics. warm-pool fill rate lagging by ~45s vs target. Autoscaler scaled nodes but GPUs not ready fast enough.
Sam: Any idea why warm-pool didn't prefill? We had prewarm=20 configured for that fleet.
Olivia: Prewarm window looks fine, but recent evictions + image pull storms slowed node readiness. Also inter-region routing sent extra traffic to us-west-2 when eu-central had a brief network blip.
Priya: Interesting — so this was a cascade: eu blip -> reroute -> regional surge -> warm-pool starvation + slow readiness -> queueing. Can we confirm admission controller behavior? Did it try shedding or just reject at threshold?
autoscale-bot: admission_controller: mode=reject, threshold_q=200, current_q=420, rejects=132, last_scale_event=2026-03-17T09:11:49Z
Marc: We were on a hard reject policy (reject at q>200). That caused a spike in 429s. Maybe we should try soft-shedding/queue-priority instead of hard rejects for these cross-region surges.
Sam: Proposal: an "adaptive-stepdown" warmup mode. Instead of prewarming fixed count, step up warm-pool aggressively on rising enqueue rate but step down slower (hysteresis). Also add a short queue-shedding policy that prioritizes best-effort traces.
Priya: I sketched a small config patch we could canary in us-west-2:

```
admission:
  mode: adaptive
  threshold_high: 180
  threshold_low: 60
  stepup_multiplier: 1.8
  stepdown_backoff: 3m
warm_pool:
  prewarm_base: 12
  prewarm_max: 60
  fill_strategy: aggressive_ramp
  node_probe_timeout: 30s
queue_shedding:
  enabled: true
  pct_shed_at_high: 20
  priority_tags: [internal, paid]
```

Olivia: Love it. A few notes: make `node_probe_timeout` conservative — image pulls were main culprit; maybe prefer faster node reuse / keepalive rather than spinning up from scratch.
Ryan: Another lever: route-level hedging for high-p99 endpoints (2nd replica after 60ms) during suspected region stress. Costly but limits tail.
Zara: For cost tradeoffs, we should track incremental GPU-hours from aggressive ramp + hedging vs value of lowered 429s. Add a metric slice for the canary.
Marc: Agreed. Also, add a small circuit-breaker to limit cross-region reroute rate so we don't amplify transient faults.
Sam: Who wants to own the canary rollout? I can push the config to us-west-2 canary pool and monitor for 2h.
Priya: I will prepare PromQL dashboards: queue_len by fleet, admission_rejects, node_ready_latency, incremental_gpu_hours. Also add synthetic sanity traffic to validate prioritization.
Olivia: Plan sounds good. If 2h canary shows reduced rejects and stable latency, roll to remaining fleets with a 10% step increase per region. If not, revert.
autoscale-bot: canary_deploy: region=us-west-2, pool=canary-adaptive-stepdown, start=1881239999, watch_window=2h
Zara: Note: update runbooks with steps to flip stepdown_backoff and disabling hedging if cost exceeds threshold.
Marc: I'll add circuit-breaker for cross-region reroutes (rate-limit per minute) and a rollback flag. Sam, coordinate the deploy time with infra maintenance window.
Sam: On it. Deploying in 10m from now — will ping here with short status updates. :rocket:
Olivia: Thanks team — let's keep the initial window tight and metrics-first. If anyone sees weird pod churn, pause immediately.
Sam: 1st status: canary applied, warm-pool started ramping. will report back in 5m.
Ryan: thumbs on the circuit-breaker PR. I'll standby for emergency rollback.
Sam: 5m: queue_len stabilized 140 -> 90 over 4m, rejects down from 132 to 18. Node ready latency still ~28s (better). Will monitor cost impact.
Olivia: Nice — keep the canary running. Good job. :thumbsup:
